<action type="say">
Here’s a tight script and what to have in front of you so the call is quick and calm.

--------------------------------
1) Info to have in front of you
--------------------------------
Have this ready before you dial:

- Your full name: Danielle Kim  
- Phone: 713-555-2847  
- Email: danielle.kim@example.com  
- Lost card details:
  - “My main credit card with your bank, last 4 digits 4321” (if they differ, they’ll tell you)
- Last known transactions (optional but helpful):
  - Rough idea of your last 1–3 legitimate purchases on that card (place + approximate amount + date)
- Personal verification:
  - Last 4 of SSN (if applicable in your country), or other ID they usually use  
  - Date of birth  
  - Your current mailing address (so you can confirm it’s correct on their screen)  

--------------------------------
2) What to say to the phone system (IVR)
--------------------------------
When you call the main customer service number:

If there’s voice menu, say:
- “Report lost credit card”  
If it asks what type of card:
- “Credit card”  

If it’s button-based, choose:
- Option close to: “Card services” → then “Lost or stolen card” or “Credit cards”.

--------------------------------
3) Script for the human rep
--------------------------------
Once a person answers, you can basically read this:

“Hi, my name is Danielle Kim. I need to report my main credit card ending in 4321 as lost and have a replacement sent to my mailing address on file. The card is lost, not stolen, and I’d like it blocked immediately and reissued.”

If they ask for details, you can add:
“I no longer have the physical card with me, but I still have access to the mobile app and my other accounts with you.”

--------------------------------
4) Questions they’re likely to ask you
--------------------------------
They’ll move through some combination of:

Identity verification:
- “Can I have your full name as it appears on the account?”
- “What is your date of birth?”
- “Can you confirm the last 4 digits of your Social Security Number (or other ID)?”
- “What’s the best phone number on your profile?”
- “What is your current mailing address?”

Account/card verification:
- “Which card are you calling about today?”
  - Answer: “My main credit card ending in 4321.”
- “Is the card lost, stolen, or damaged?”
  - Answer: “Lost.”
- “When did you notice it was missing?”
  - Give approximate date/time.

Fraud/suspicious charges:
- “Do you see any transactions you don’t recognize?”
  - If yes: have 1–2 examples ready (merchant, date, approximate amount).
  - If no: “So far I don’t see anything suspicious, but I’d like you to keep an eye on it.”

Replacement details:
- “Do you want a replacement card sent to your address on file?”
  - Answer: “Yes.”
- “Can you please confirm your mailing address?”
  - Read your current address exactly as it should appear.
- “Do you need the replacement expedited?”
  - If you care: “If there’s an option to expedite, please tell me the fee and delivery time.”

--------------------------------
5) What to confirm before you hang up
--------------------------------
Right near the end, say:

“Before we wrap up, can you confirm:
1) The lost card ending in 4321 is completely blocked and can’t be used anymore.  
2) A replacement card has been ordered.  
3) What date I should expect it to arrive by.  
4) Whether my card number will change, and if so, whether any automatic payments I have set up will be affected.”

If you know you have subscriptions on that card, you can add:
“I have some recurring charges on that card — will they keep going through, or do I need to update them once the new card arrives?”

--------------------------------
6) If they mention suspicious transactions
--------------------------------
If they say they see anything odd, you can respond:

“I don’t recognize that transaction; please treat it as unauthorized and open a dispute. Can you send me a summary of the dispute and next steps by email or in the app?”

---

If you want, tell me roughly when you last had the card and whether you’ve seen any weird transactions in your app, and I’ll help you phrase answers for that part, too.</action>
